What day is the Fisherman's Village Walking Street? | The main Fisherman's Village Walking Street is every Friday evening on Bophut's beach road. Smaller, quieter markets also run on Monday and Wednesday evenings. If you only have one evening, choose Friday, when the market stretches the whole length of the village from The Wharf to Coco Tam's.
What time does the Fisherman's Village market start and finish? | It runs from about 17:00 to 23:00 on Fridays, with stalls setting up from about 16:00 and the road closing to traffic from about 16:30. It is busiest from about 19:00 to 20:30. Arrive at 17:30–18:00 to park easily and eat before the crowds.
Where do I park for the Friday market in Bophut? | The car park at The Wharf is the easiest, but it fills by about 18:00 on Fridays; paid lots on the side lanes fill too. Park scooters only in marked bays, because scooters left on the closed road are towed or clamped. Coming by Grab or taxi saves the hassle altogether.
Is there a Fisherman's Village market on other nights? | Yes. Smaller markets run on Monday and Wednesday evenings from about 17:00, and the Free Wave Market by the Fisherman's Village sign opens daily from about 16:00 to midnight. The organic Samui Green Market is held on the last Sunday of each month, from about 15:00 to 19:00.
What food is at the Fisherman's Village market and what does it cost? | Expect Thai street food at 2026 prices of about 40 THB for papaya salad, 60–80 for pad thai, 80–120 for grilled prawns, around 10 per satay stick and 50–80 for mango sticky rice. A full dinner with a drink costs about 300–500 THB per person. Bring cash.
Is the Fisherman's Village Walking Street suitable for children? | Yes. The road is closed to cars, there is plenty of child-friendly food, and the fire shows at Coco Tam's are popular with kids. Go between 17:00 and 18:30, when it is cooler and quieter, use a carrier rather than a stroller after 19:00, and agree a meeting point such as The Wharf entrance.
How do I get to Fisherman's Village from Chaweng or Lamai? | From Chaweng, a Grab costs about 80–120 THB off-peak, and a songthaew about 40–50 THB for locals (tourists are often asked 60–80). From Lamai, budget about 200–350 THB by Grab and allow extra time for Chaweng traffic. Songthaews mostly stop by 22:00, so plan your ride home.
Does the Fisherman's Village market run in the rain? | It runs all year, but heavy rain can close many stalls, especially from October to December during the north-east monsoon. Showers are often short, so check the forecast and radar before setting off. The covered restaurants and The Wharf stay open in the rain.
